?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:13754
Court No. - 15
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 3109 of 2023

Applicant :- Aftab Ahmad And Another
Opposite Party :- Central Bureau Of Investigation, Anti-Corruption Branch, Lucknow

Counsel for Applicant :- Himanshu Hemant Gupta
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anurag Kumar Singh
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
1.
Heard Mr. Himanshu Hemant Gupta, learned counsel for the applicants, as well as Mr. Anurag Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the respondent- CBI, and perused the record.
Counter affidavit, filed on behalf of the respondent- CBI, is taken on record.

2. This application has been moved by the applicants- Aftab Ahmad and Mohammad Zakariya for grant of anticipatory bail in Session Case No.491 of 2023, arising out of RC0062011A0007, under Sections 120-B, 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC and Sections 13(2) read with Sections 13(1)(d) P.C. Act lodged at Police Station SPE/ACB, Lucknow.
3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that it is a case of false implication.
The applicants were not named in the FIR and during the course of investigation their culpability is shown to have occurred in the crime.

It is further submitted that the FIR of this case has been registered by the CBI Aftab Ahmad And Another vs Central Bureau Of Investigation, ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53124044/
1 on 13.04.2011 against named accused persons and some unknown officers/officials of district industries centre, district Chandauli and officers/officials of northern coal fields limited alleging that certain illegalities have been committed in supplying coal by the officers/officials of northern coal fields limited and a huge amount has been misappropriated in connivance with the officers/officials of district industries centre.

entities.text: CBI Aftab Ahmad And Another vs Central Bureau Of Investigation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. It is further submitted that during the course of investigation the role of the applicants is alleged to the tune that they are the owners of M/s Pahalwan Transport Company and during the year 2010-2011 sale of about 816.86 metric ton of SSF and 219.21 metric tons of undersized coal was shown to have been made to the company of the applicants by M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd.
through 55 and 14 truck-loads.

It is vehemently submitted that without there being any sufficient evidence/material the charge-sheet had been submitted by the CBI and thereafter the Directorate of Enforcement has started investigation in the matter.

It is further submitted that in the year 2007 the Ministry of Coal had come with a new coal distribution policy and fuel supply agreements, which were entered into between the NCL and coal companies and the said agreements were binding and enforceable qua the parties and there was a specific penalty clause under these agreements and when the penalty clause was provided in the contract itself, initiation of criminal proceedings is bad and, therefore, any alleged breach of the agreement committed by theM/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd.
cannot be a criminal offence and initiation of any criminal proceeding on such breach of agreement is a sheer abuse of process of the law.
5.

It is also submitted that the primary allegations against the applicants are to the tune that they were purchasers of coal from M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. and, therefore, the relevant provisions of sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC and sections 13(2) read with Sections 13(1)(d) P.C. Act could only be attracted against the director of M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. and the DIC officials as the applicants were only the bona fide purchasers of coal from M/s Shree Ram Fuels Pvt. Ltd. and also they were not a party to the said agreements and in fact they were not having any knowledge of the said agreements or any of their condition at that point of time.

It is further submitted that the applicants after filing of the charge-sheet had approached this Court by filing a petition under Section 482 CrPC No. 5013 of 2012 and vide order dated 21.11.2012 were granted interim order and the said petition was connected with a bunch of petitions and the interim order dated 21.11.2012 was extended from time to time and was confirmed by the Court vide order dated 24.02.2015 and the matter was referred to the division bench of this court.
It is further submitted that vide another order dated 14.08.2019 the petition under Section 482 CrPC No. 5013 of 2012 was dismissed.

6. It is vehemently submitted that during the course of investigation the applicants have cooperated in the investigation and had remained present before the investigating officer as and when their presence was required and since the charge-sheet has been submitted, the applicants would also cooperate in the trial as they have cooperated in the investigation.

It is also submitted that co-accused persons, namely, Ravindra Aggarwal and Gajraj Kunwar Jain have been granted anticipatory bail vide orders passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Nos. 857 of 2023 and 1696 of 2023 and one of the co-accused person- Ramji Singh has also been granted anticipatory bail vide order passed in criminal misc. anticipatory bail application no.676 of 2023.

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that since the applicants have not been arrested by the investigating agency and they have Aftab Ahmad And Another vs Central Bureau Of Investigation, ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53124044/
2 cooperated in the investigation, the interim protection order was granted in their favour, which they have not misused, the facility of anticipatory bail be provided to them.

sentences.text: 7. Mr. Anurag Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the respondent- CBI, opposes the prayer of the applicants for grant of anticipatory bail but could not dispute the fact that the applicants have cooperated in the investigation, they were not named in the FIR and also that many other co-accused persons have been granted anticipatory bail.

8. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is reflected that the applicants have cooperated in the investigation throughout and the charge-sheet has been filed without making their arrest.
The applicants are not named in the FIR.
It is also surfaced that this matter remained pending before this Court in various jurisdictions and ultimately the trial started before the trial Court.

The applicants on approaching this Court were granted interim protection order dated 22.12.2023 subject to certain conditions and nothing has been brought before this Court which may suggest that the applicants have violated any of the conditions under which their personal liberty was protected.

Thus, having regard to all the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping an eye on the specific circumstance that during the course of investigation the applicants were not arrested by the investigating agency, the facility of anticipatory bail may safely be extended to them on merits as well as on principle of parity as various co-accused persons, including Ramji Singh, have been granted the facility of anticipatory bail.
9. Thus, the instant anticipatory bail application moved on behalf of the applicants-Aftab Ahmad and Mohammad Zakariya is allowed and the interim protection order dated 22.12.2023 is made absolute.

It is provided that in the event of arrest of the applicants under any process of the trial Court or on their appearance/surrender before the trial Court within 20 days from today i.e. till 05.03.2024, whichever is earlier, they shall be released forthwith on anticipatory bail on each of them furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, subject to the following conditions:-
(i). The applicants, if not arrested earlier, shall appear before the trial court within 20 days from today i.e. till 05.03.2024 and cooperate in the trial and shall not seek any adjournment when the prosecution witness would be in attendance.

( ii). In case of further investigation or re-investigation the applicants shall cooperate in the investigation and make themselves available as and when required by the Investigating officer of the case, even for the recovery of any fact.
(iii). The applicants shall not make any attempt to influence the prosecution witnesses and will also not commit any crime during their release on anticipatory bail.

(iv). The applicants shall file an undertaking to the effect that they shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence and specially when the prosecution witnesses are present in court.

3 (v).

sentences.text:
The applicants shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
10.
The personal bond as well as surety bonds, if filed by the applicants and are sufficient in the opinion of the trial Court, the applicants no need to file the same again.

11. If in the opinion of the trial court default of any of the condition placed above is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and shall proceed against him/her in accordance with law.
12. It is clarified that all the observations contained in this order are only for disposal of this anticipatory bail application and shall not affect the trial proceedings in any manner.
